a.xlink:title: WCAG relative luminance of an opaque color.
WCAG contrast ratio between two opaque colors, from 1.0 to 21.0.
The harder of two surfaces to keep an ink legible on.
Pushes color away from background until it reaches minRatio.
Every shipped theme keeps the disabled level below the quiet level.
A disabled glyph recedes past the quiet level, whatever the family.
Quiet is the least chromatic level; it shares the legibility floor.
Resolves the concrete color for an icon mode.
Palette tints keep the WindowText -> HighlightedText selected swap.
A medium-light surface needs the pole that can actually reach the floor.
The System fallback family keeps the ladder on a platform palette.
Primary stays louder than secondary on a light surface.
Every palette-shipping theme authors the whole emphasis ladder.
The authored primary level is the most chromatic member of its family.
The ink a disabled glyph is painted with, given the quiet level.
Icon ink for a neutral glyph, given the palette it is drawn from.
Writes the authored emphasis sheets for every shipped palette theme.
A green or red accent must not tint neutral chrome.
Writes the glyph-ink comparison sheet when asked; skipped otherwise.
Disabled keeps the shape language but drops back to the line glyph.
Disabled keeps the shape language but drops back to the line glyph.
Emphasis selects the authored variant of a family, not a computed color.
A line glyph renders the authored role verbatim.
A selected row falls back to HighlightedText when the tint vanishes.
A selected row keeps a semantic tint that still contrasts enough.
A semantic tint must paint its theme color, not the selection accent.
The pixmap API's badge path agrees with the engine's.
The pixmap API's sticker path agrees with the engine's.
A badge is a disc with a gradient fill, a dark ring and a contrast glyph.
Badge never paints authored art: the asset keeps its own colors.
The player list is the one place the badge has to work, at 15px.
Line stays the default: no disc, no ring, just the recolored glyph.
Sticker never paints authored art: the asset keeps its own colors.
Sticker fills the glyph with the tone and rims it with a dark outline.
A sticker has to survive the 16px toolbar slot.
Renders a resolved theme SVG when it carries the currentColor sentinel.
